text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER — Detecting elevated 5xx rate and tail latency for variant gptx-canary-2026-quant in us-west-2. Thresholds tripped at 1729987654. Paging @oncall-alex.

oncall-alex: ack — I'm on it, grabbing dashboards and logs.

sre-maya: joining. I see 95p latency jump and token-level 503s. QPS hasn't increased, so likely runtime/serving issue rather than traffic burst.

eng-runtime-jordan: I can roll traffic if we need to protect customers. Suggest dial back canary weight to 0% and rehome to stable-1.7 while we debug.

oncall-alex: quick check — prefix cache miss rate up ~40% for this variant, memory pressure on the quant instances looks suspicious.

eng-runtime-jordan: runbook step (routing):
```
# set variant weight to 0 to stop routing to canary
curl -X POST https://control-plane.redwood/api/v1/routing \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"gptx","variant":"gptx-canary-2026-quant","weight":0}'
```
I'll hand this off to SRE to execute if oncall wants.

sre-maya: I'll apply the routing change and also add emergency per-key quotas for the noisy keys. Listing heavy keys now: acct-820, acct-311, acct-449.

sre-maya: applying temporary quotas: `quota.set("acct-820", "rps", 10)` `quota.set("acct-311", "rps", 5)` `quota.set("acct-449", "rps", 5)` — pushed.

ops-bot: :gear: rollout started — rehoming traffic off gptx-canary-2026-quant to stable-1.7 (pool: stable-1.7-usw2, nodes: 5). Change id: rollout-1729987654-01. ETA ~60s.

oncall-alex: routing change applied, canary weight -> 0. Monitoring dashboards.

sre-maya: observing error rate dropping already. 60s after change, 5xx down from ~6% to ~0.9%. 95p latency trending down.

eng-runtime-jordan: canary hosts are in drain but still reporting OOM in logs. I'll enable circuit-breaker on canary host group to stop new connections: `cb.set("gptx-canary-2026-quant", true)`

oncall-alex: circuit-breaker enabled. Confirming no new sessions hitting canary.

pm-tereza: I started a customer-impact draft for CS and Status page: short blurb indicating service degradation for a canary variant, mitigation in place, and that we're investigating. Will share for review.

sre-maya: collecting logs and core dumps from canary instances, preserving artifacts under INF-4521. Running the standard repro harness against the quant library to try to reproduce memory blowup.

eng-runtime-jordan: preliminary hypothesis: quant kernel allocator regression introduced in libquant v0.10. Rolling back quant lib on a single canary node to v0.9.2 for repro and safe test. If stable, we'll re-run a controlled canary at 1% weight.

incident-bot: Incident status update — Mitigated: traffic removed from gptx-canary-2026-quant and rehomed to stable-1.7. Severity lowered to Sev2. Pager cleared for on-call.

oncall-alex: handoff: @sre-maya will own remediation and artifact collection; @eng-runtime-jordan will continue root-cause analysis on quant kernel. I'll move to monitoring-only and update the incident ticket with actions taken.

pm-tereza: please include a customer impact summary (approx # of affected requests, timeframe, keys throttled) in the postmortem. We'll coordinate CS comms after the RCA draft.

sre-maya: noted — impact estimate: ~2.2k failed requests over 6 minutes for canary routing 10% traffic slice across us-west-2; heavy keys limited to reduce blast radius. Tagging all artifacts INF-4521.

oncall-alex: final mitigation list for ticket: routing weight -> 0, emergency quotas applied to heavy keys, circuit-breaker enabled on canary hosts, customer comms drafted, logs + cores collected. Leaving handoff.

incident-bot: Pager cleared. Please remember to run postmortem and attach timeline + runbook gaps. :white_check_mark:
